svg.title: Allocate a $30,000 Reference Launch Budget
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-thirty-thousand-reference-startup-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate a $30,000 Reference Launch Budget; subtitle: Four buckets reconcile $10,000 lean, $30,000 reference, and $50,000 expanded plans.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: All amounts are USD. Numeric values encode only the $30,000 central/reference startup stack within the canonical $10,000–$50,000 startup capital range. The value text supplies comparable $10,000 lean and $50,000 expanded stacks in the same four-bucket order. These are startup cash allocations, not annual expenses or revenue scenarios. Do not stack all three budgets together.; caption: Lean: $3,000 + $1,500 + $500 + $5,000 = $10,000. Reference: $8,000 + $3,500 + $1,500 + $17,000 = $30,000. Expanded: $13,000 + $6,000 + $3,000 + $28,000 = $50,000. A lean launch uses existing transport and staged commitments. None of these budgets guarantees runway for the four-person core pod (1 FT + 3 C), external delivery crews, or expansion to six people (2 FT + 4 C); model mobilization and collections.; stages: label: Equipment and initial supplies; value: Lean $3,000; reference $8,000; expanded $13,000 equipment cash; numeric value: 8000.0; detail: Allocate $3,000 lean, $8,000 reference, or $13,000 expanded to commercial vacuums, carts, microfiber systems, PPE, dispensers, and initial chemicals. Rent infrequent specialty machines until contracted utilization supports ownership. Avoid duplicating client-provided or independent provider-owned equipment in the budget.; label: Setup and coverage deposits; value: Lean $1,500; reference $3,500; expanded $6,000 setup cash; numeric value: 3500.0; detail: Allocate $1,500 lean, $3,500 reference, or $6,000 expanded to registration, required local licensing, insurance deposits, contract preparation, and initial safety training. Replace estimates with jurisdiction-specific fees and written broker quotations before committing funds.; label: Acquisition and operating systems; value: Lean $500; reference $1,500; expanded $3,000 acquisition cash; numeric value: 1500.0; detail: Allocate $500 lean, $1,500 reference, or $3,000 expanded to a focused website, local prospect research, walkthrough travel, estimating setup, and appropriately staged Swept and QuickBooks configuration. Limit subscription seats and advertising commitments until the first route converts.; label: Payroll and collection buffer; value: Lean $5,000; reference $17,000; expanded $28,000 liquidity; numeric value: 17000.0; detail: Hold $5,000 lean, $17,000 reference, or $28,000 expanded as unspent cash for wages, payroll charges, subcontract invoices, and collection delays. At Base-Case direct service labor of $435,000 yearly, the $17,000 reference buffer covers about two weeks of that cost alone. External vendor/trade sub-crews are direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through, not internal pod headcount. Stage mobilization and model all other cash outflows separately.

rect.title: label: Equipment and initial supplies; numeric value: 8000.0; value: Lean $3,000; reference $8,000; expanded $13,000 equipment cash; detail: Allocate $3,000 lean, $8,000 reference, or $13,000 expanded to commercial vacuums, carts, microfiber systems, PPE, dispensers, and initial chemicals. Rent infrequent specialty machines until contracted utilization supports ownership. Avoid duplicating client-provided or independent provider-owned equipment in the budget.

Replace estimates with jurisdiction-specific fees and written broker quotations before committing funds.

Limit subscription seats and advertising commitments until the first route converts.

At Base-Case direct service labor of $435,000 yearly, the $17,000 reference buffer covers about two weeks of that cost alone. External vendor/trade sub-crews are direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through, not internal pod headcount. Stage mobilization and model all other cash outflows separately.
